turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
"Oh, hi. Sure, ready when you are."
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Around half past ten, like usual."
Thanks. Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night, and would you say you slept well? Why or why not?
"About six, maybe six and a half — I woke up around four again and couldn't quite drop back off. I'd say it was fine, not great. It's not really bad sleep, it's just... light, these days."
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?
"Reading, actually. Just on my phone, nothing serious — usually just news or something silly to wind down. Doesn't take long before I'm ready to turn the light off."
What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

"Honestly, the early waking is the main thing — same as always. Work's been steady, nothing stressful, and my husband's evening shifts mean we don't overlap much, so the house is already quiet by the time I go up. Nothing dramatic, really."
Is waking up early like this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently in how you're sleeping?
"Pretty typical, yeah. Been like this for a couple of years now — I just figure it's part of getting older, honestly. Nothing's really changed recently, it's just... how my sleep goes now."
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?
"Fine, honestly. It's not perfect, but it's not something I lose sleep over, if you'll pardon the joke. At this point I've made peace with it — it's just how my body works now."
Thanks for explaining that. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

"Honestly? Not really, no. If I got seven hours I'd be thrilled, but between the four a.m. wake-up and needing to be up by six for work, it's more like six, six and a half most nights. I've stopped chasing the number, if I'm honest."
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?
"Not really, no. Once I put it down after my little scroll, that's it — I'm not one to lie there scrolling for ages. Habit, I suppose, more than anything deliberate."
Do you regularly use social media? If so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
"Not much, honestly — I look at Facebook now and then to see photos from the kids, but it's a quick check, not a habit before bed. I'm usually more interested in winding down than scrolling."
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications?
"No, not really — I've heard of them, my kids talk about that stuff, but I haven't used them myself. Not my thing, I suppose."
Thanks for explaining that. If you think about your sleep over the time since social media and these newer technologies have become common, do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all?
"Not really, to be honest — my sleep's about the same as it's always been. It changed a bit years ago when the kids were small, but that had nothing to do with phones or any of that."
Thanks for sharing that. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

"Getting back to sleep after that four a.m. wake-up, that's the one thing. I've made peace with the early waking itself, but if I could just drop off again for another hour instead of dozing on and off, that'd be nice."

Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that change—being able to get back to sleep after waking at four—would be doable? Why or why not?

(Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.) After that, I’ll ask a final short set of background questions.

"Doable, sure, but I'm not going to hold my breath for it. I'm not stressed enough about it to change my routine over — it hasn't really cost me at work, so I'd rather just live with it than fuss over it."

Thanks, that makes sense. Now for that final short set of background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.)

Could you tell me your age?
"Fifty-two."
Thank you. What is your profession?
"Quality control inspector — at an appliance manufacturer, so I check units coming off the line before they ship."
Thank you. Which country were you born in?
Slovenia.
Thanks. Which country do you currently live in?
"Slovenia — same as where I was born, just moved to Ljubljana for work."

Thanks for clarifying that. Those were all the main questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep or nightly routine that you’d like to add that we didn’t talk about?
